subject: Request: short-term POC credits for burst throughput / SLA probe
messages:
From: Steve Harris <steve.harris@finlytics.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finlytics.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC request — short burst run for throughput validation

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to run a short, high-concurrency load window to validate latency and throughput under production-like inputs before we commit to a Dedicated config. Specifically: 24–48 hours of sustained bursts (~500 concurrent requests, average prompt length ~600 tokens) to validate tail latency and KV cache behavior.

Can Redwood provide a temporary credit top-up or trial extension to cover this run? We estimate ~150k–200k tokens based on our tooling but can share the test plan.

Attached: finlytics_poc_test_plan.pdf

Key constraints:
- Run window target: Wed 2027-08-04 00:00 UTC for 24–48 hours (flexible)
- Need per-token billing waiver or temporary promo credits on our trial account DL-4812-FIN
- We will share logs and a short report afterward for joint analysis

Appreciate a quick confirmation — procurement may need a short note for internal approval.

Best,
Steve Harris
Head of Engineering
FinLytics

Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700

Hi Steve,

Thanks for the details — this sounds reasonable. I'm looping in our performance leads and our solutions engineer to size this and propose a short promo credit we can apply to your trial account.

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: POC request — short burst run for throughput validation

Team — forwarding a POC ask from FinLytics. They want a short 24–48h burst (500 concurrent, ~600-token prompts). They asked for a promo/top-up to the trial account to cover ~150k–200k tokens.

Can you:
1) Jonas — confirm whether the requested run looks safe for a hosted trial account and give a realistic token estimate and any recommended model/config (e.g., Redwood-medium-8q/quantization profile).
2) Priyom — propose the exact promo amount you'd request and the success criteria we should include (latency / 99th percentile target / canary fallback).

If we can keep this to a single promotional grant (no contractual changes), I'd like to approve quickly. Marissa — tagging you for revenue/credit approval once we have numbers.

Thanks,
Irene
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: POC request — short burst run for throughput validation

Irene / Priyom — quick engineering readout after scanning the test plan:
- The workload is IO-heavy but within expected patterns. Recommended model: rwd-medium-v2-quant (cost-efficient, supports the KV prefix cache we need).
- Estimated token consumption: ~165k tokens for a 24-hour burst at the concurrency you describe; ~320k tokens for 48 hours. Margin of error +-10%.
- Operational caveats: keep the session durations < 10s where possible to avoid large KV blowups; enable prefix cache TTL for repeated prompts; set a per-client rate cap to protect other trial users.

I attached a quick perf estimate CSV with assumptions. If we greenlight a single promo grant, 200k tokens should cover a safer 24–36h run and supply a buffer for retries.

Attachments: redwood_perf_estimate.csv

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Steve Harris <steve.harris@finlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: POC request — short burst run for throughput validation

Thanks Jonas — +1 on the numbers. My operational proposal:
- Grant: 200,000 promo tokens applied to FinLytics trial account DL-4812-FIN
- Run window: 2027-08-04 00:00 UTC — target 24h, optional extension to 36h if metrics look clean
- Success criteria (joint): 99th percentile latency under 450ms for the targeted model and no >5% error spikes; Redwood will provide streaming logs and a post-run summary within 48h.
- Fallbacks: automatic rollback to a smaller model if we see GPU memory pressure; manual throttle knob for FinLytics to reduce concurrency.

If Revenue is comfortable with the promotional spend we can apply the credits now and confirm the schedule with Steve.

— Priyom
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
